title: Mobile apps FAQ
claim: Store-distributed native apps depend on compatible hosted push; self-hosting the push service requires compatible custom mobile builds.
limitations: Specific to Mattermost native app distribution; does not establish constraints for standards-based Web Push. Some FAQ prose is broader than current encrypted-payload alternatives.

title: Configure Mobile Settings and Push Notifications
claim: Community hosted push allowance is 10,000 notifications monthly; custom delivery requires credentials, infrastructure and compatible clients.
limitations: Limits and plan entitlements can change. Gateway allowance is not a server user limit.

title: Get started with Rocket.Chat
claim: Starter is free up to 50 users and lists unlimited push; Community has different capabilities and push limits.
limitations: Vendor product page, not an independent reliability assessment or enforceability audit of every edition.

title: Self-hosted Zulip billing
claim: Free hosted push supports up to 10 users; qualifying communities can apply for free unlimited push; the self-hosted server remains freely usable without a plan.
limitations: Community eligibility is reviewed; do not assume every group qualifies. Published service terms are time-sensitive.

title: Web Push for Web Apps on iOS and iPadOS
publisher: WebKit / Brady Eidson and Jen Simmons
claim: Home Screen web apps can receive push with user permission; Apple Developer Program membership is unnecessary.
limitations: Launch-era platform documentation; actual current devices and permission flows still require testing.

title: ONCE — Campfire
claim: Campfire currently advertises MIT distribution, mobile PWA push/badges and optional automatic updates; its import FAQ says no Slack/Teams import.
limitations: Product claims, not a reproduced usability or capacity study. Current free distribution should not be confused with earlier purchase pricing.

title: Mobile push notification service
claim: Zulip documents server-to-device encrypted notification contents, metadata exposure and mobile push registration migration.
limitations: Latest development documentation may lead released behavior; encrypted push does not hide content from the workspace server.

title: Quick Tunnels
claim: Quick Tunnels generate random subdomains, provide no uptime SLA and are for testing; current limit is 200 in-flight requests.
limitations: Not a concurrent-user capacity figure and not the terms for named Cloudflare Tunnels.

title: Service Workers Nightly
claim: Service-worker registration requires trustworthy origins and same-origin script/scope/referrer relationships.
limitations: Normative browser model; installed-PWA address-migration implications are our inference, not a Tandem implementation test.

title: Preparing an ESS Pro PoC
claim: Matrix server-name identity is chosen before install and cannot be changed without resetting the database; deployment needs explicit domain and certificate planning.
limitations: ESS Pro requirements are not minimum requirements for every Matrix deployment or for Tandem.

title: Backup and disaster recovery
claim: Recovery includes database, configuration and files; stopping is recommended for consistency; backups, HA and disaster recovery are distinct.
limitations: Instructions depend on storage and deployment mode; cloud object storage durability alone is not a universal recovery guarantee.

title: Backups, export and import
claim: Full backups include settings/secrets and local uploads; restore compatibility and external storage exclusions differ from logical export.
limitations: Latest development docs; Docker and standard installation backup units differ. Not a claim that every operator follows them.

title: Backup and Restore
claim: ESS Pro recovery inventory includes database, chart values, generated secrets, deployment markers and media.
limitations: Specific to ESS Pro Helm deployment; does not imply all Matrix users need Kubernetes.

title: Version Durability
claim: Standard releases have six-month support and LTS twelve; EOL affects cloud services and may affect official client connectivity.
limitations: Policy is version- and time-sensitive; this is not a claim that the local server deletes data at EOL.

title: Upgrade Zulip
claim: Upgrade-time memory can exceed runtime needs; simple rollback is intended for minor releases and schema downgrades require more care.
limitations: Development documentation and installation-path-specific guidance, not a measured Tandem resource requirement.

title: Migrate off Bitnami images before Aug 28 (memcached/postgresql/rabbitmq/redis)
publisher: zulip/docker-zulip issue participants and maintainer alexmv
claim: A maintainer explains Bitnami Helm templates cannot simply use stock RabbitMQ/Redis images and points to end-to-end deployment tests.
limitations: Read issue and replies via GitHub REST after HTML fetch failures. Helm dependency path only; not all Zulip installations. Date is latest returned update.

title: Resolved: MISSING_MATRIX_RTC_TRANSPORT on self-hosted MatrixRTC/LiveKit
publisher: Element X Android issue reporter and commenters
claim: A failure initially reported as a client regression was resolved by adding newer homeserver transport configuration; a commenter reports deployment upgrade helped.
limitations: One deployment report; not prevalence evidence. Title says resolved while issue remains open. Read body and resolution/comments via GitHub REST.

title: Mattermost Calls Deployment Guide
claim: Signalling and media have separate network requirements; TURN is fallback; integrated and dedicated media deployments have different prerequisites.
limitations: Current edition/licensing choices are vendor-specific and do not define Tandem architectural limits.

title: Self-Hosting Element Call
claim: Current MatrixRTC deployment requires LiveKit SFU and authorization service with client-reachable routing.
limitations: Main-branch documentation can change and can lead released clients. Legacy Element/Jitsi documentation differs.

title: No instruction on docker images
claim: Operator describes public-versus-local media URL confusion and standalone container configuration difficulty despite working in-app calls.
limitations: One historical setup report, not proof that current instructions or all deployments fail.

title: Mattermost Calls drops connection due to internal Docker IP used as ICE candidate
claim: Reporter describes sustained-call failure involving Docker/private candidates and coturn despite a standalone TURN check succeeding.
limitations: Closed as not planned when opened; root cause not independently confirmed. Use as test scenario, not established product-wide defect.

title: Export your workspace data
claim: Export coverage depends on plan/approval and contains file links; current Free export file links cover the last 90 days.
limitations: Source export limitations do not prove which attachments a particular authorized migration can retrieve.

title: Import from Slack
claim: Importer handles mapped identities, roles and thread/topic conversion; settings and passwords do not transfer; import targets a new organization.
limitations: Vendor-supported workflow, not an independent fidelity audit; detailed implementation and current version may differ.

title: Slack importer: thread-to-topic conversion and import-robustness bugs
claim: Code-audit report lists chunk-boundary threads, malformed timestamps, unusual names and file metadata as import failure cases.
limitations: Reported code findings not independently reproduced; do not assume all remain unfixed or affect all import paths.
